chapter: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
title: Taking over the high-school boys' band with Roy Milton and Eddie Nicholson
summary: The group with Roy Milton and Roy Randall makes Fields leader; he again turns down Foots' Cab Calloway offer, tours Kansas, and hires Eddie Nicholson on drums.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Later on, when they changed it from the Missourians, they contacted me again, but at that time I had then started with this

little group, that I told you when I was going on the trouble calls, a bunch of high school boys. I think one young man wasn't in high school, but it was Roy Milton. Roy Milton was drummer and Roy Randall was the leader who is now (inaudible). He was the leader of the bunch and Oscar Warner was in the group, Booker--I'm getting mixed up--but anyway none of them turned out to be well known other than Roy Milton, as far as that group. I went on to play with them.
So we played a while, when Roy Randall, who was the leader, he said let's let him be the leader, he seems to know a little more about music than we do.
Yes, talking about me. And all the others said yeah, that's okay, they all went for it.
So then that's where I had taken them over. So when Foots called me then about this Cab Calloway, he said it's going to be sensational, you better come on now, because he

said something about we're going east, they won't be trying to get anybody back this way after then and you'll be right in on the ground floor. I told Foots, well, no, I started with these little boys, but it might work up to something, Walt, and I believe I'll stick with it along with my little job for a while yet. So he said okay and went on and I turned that down. So we just played around and we would gig and so finally I got a gig up in--a guy by the name of Lloyd White--I forget how he got in touch with me or something, but the reputation that there's this little band in Tulsa and they'll travel. You see, lots of bands would play and be nice, but with their jobs they couldn't get off, and so that I could leave town. So this Lloyd contacted me and I went up to Hutchin, Kansas, we had three or four dates in that area and Wichita, and played and I met Eddie Nicholson there.
Yes, Eddie Nicholson the drummer. And he said I kind of like your band and everything (inaudible).

So Roy Milton, I had a talk with him and I told Roy, I said Roy, I'm still with you, I says, but I'm going to put you in front of the band, so you know you're all right with me, and so I put him like they called the entertainment. I put Roy Milton up there and I got Eddie Nicholson on drums.
